title: Planning and Logistics Lead
leads: The Inventory Manager, the hub attendants, and the runners. The Inventory Manager holds the store on the days you work remotely.
where: The store at the Central Cairo warehouse, the hub, and the sites on the schedule. Part of the week remotely
hours: Six days a week, part of them remote. Reachable until the last run is in at 10:00 PM
summary: You plan where every phone and person goes, and you run the store, the hub, and the runners that get them there. No phone moves without your approval.

posting.headline: Planning and Logistics Lead (schedule, store, hub, and runners), Cairo
posting.about: KMSC runs the field operations behind one of the most ambitious artificial intelligence projects in the region, at factories, warehouses, and farms across Cairo. The Planning and Logistics Lead plans every move: which devices and people go to which site, and when. You run the store, the hub, the runners, and the buying, reporting to the Director of Operations.
do: Write the dispatch schedule and the site plan for every new site: the devices, the people, and the date.
Turn the schedule into a buying list: what to buy, how many, and by when.
Buy the equipment in Egypt, deal with the suppliers, and keep spares at ten percent.
Own the store, the kits, and the device registry, with the Inventory Manager checking kit in and out under you.
Run the hub at the Central Cairo warehouse and the attendants who work it through the night.
Run the runners: the nightly plan, the spare list, the last run in by 10:00 PM, and the morning return before 7:00 AM.
need: You have run a store, a warehouse, or a team of drivers before.
Careful with a list, so every device has a row and every bag has a signature.
Good with a schedule, so you see next week's shortage today.
Calm on the phone at 9:00 PM when a runner is late, even from home.
plus: You have bought equipment in Egypt and dealt with suppliers.
You have planned people and equipment across more than one site.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Your own store, the hub, an Inventory Manager, and a team of runners and attendants.
Every procedure written down: the schedule, the kit, the hub night, the run, and the count.
A daily line to the Director of Operations, part of the week from home, and an operation growing from hundreds of people to thousands.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and the stores, fleets, or teams you have run. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Planning and Logistics Lead at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Director of Operations.
Your start date is {start}. In your first weeks you take over the store, the registry, and the hub, and you write your first dispatch schedule with {manager}.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours. Those hours need a phone on a head at the right site, a hub that empties it overnight, and a runner who brings it back by 7:00 AM. You plan every move, and no phone moves anywhere without your approval. The Inventory Manager holds the store on your remote days, but the plan, the hub, and the runners stay yours.
outcomes: Every new site launches on the day the schedule named, with a whole kit.
Every run is at the hub before 10:00 PM. Every phone is back at its site before 7:00 AM.
The registry, the MDM, and the room say the same number every Thursday.
Every phone is where the registry says, and the spare pool never falls under ten percent.
daily: Morning. Read the hub numbers sent before 7:00 AM: phones in, out, and held. A held phone is a call to its Portfolio Manager.
Morning. Check the dashboard for phones still holding footage. Change tonight's plan if a site needs a run.
All day. Every move of a phone, between sites or between floors, comes to you first. A yes gets a registry row.
Same day. The store is short, or the hub line is down. Order, or open the ticket with the ISP, now.
By 4:00 PM. Tonight's plan to every runner and attendant. A missing runner is replaced from the spare list by 6:00 PM.
10:00 PM. Every run on the plan is in, or Moharam knows which is not.
Every day. Meet Moharam with the schedule, the stock, and what is short. On a remote day, by phone.
weekly: Thursday, 4:00 PM. The weekly count at the store, every site, and the hub: registry, MDM, and room match.
Once a week. Next week's launches against the stock. Short means order today, or the date waits.
Once a week. Next week's store days and remote days to Moharam and the Inventory Manager. Check the spare runner list.
monthly: Month end. Turn next month's site plans into procurement demand. Send the buying list to Ahmed Alaa for approval.
Month end. Go through the month's runs and hub logs with the runners and attendants. Agree on what to change.
standards: The schedule names every phone and person from today's stock, never from another site's kit.
No site launches short. If the plan says short, the date waits.
No phone moves between places, or between parts of a site, without your approval and a registry row.
One attendant at the hub per night. A second when the hub takes more than 150 phones a night.
One runner for every three hub sites in the same area, with a vehicle. One spare per area.
The morning return is the same runner and the same three sites as the night before, all phones back before 7:00 AM.
On your remote days the Inventory Manager holds the store. The plan, the hub, and the runners stay yours.
Money to Ahmed Alaa, quality to Youssef Medhat, papers to Mano. Nobody contacts the client.
never: A phone that moves on a promise. Your approval and the registry row come first, every time.
A run that cannot reach the hub by 10:00 PM does not leave.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: In the store with Moharam and the Inventory Manager. The registry, the kit list, the tags, the hub, and the runner plan.
Run the Thursday count and one full hub night yourself. Write tonight's runner plan every day.
Write one dispatch schedule and site plan end to end. The Inventory Manager builds the kit. Moharam checks every phone before the handover.
One launch on the day you named, with a whole kit. One remote day, the Inventory Manager holding the store. Moharam signs you off.

measures: Launches on the day the schedule named, with a whole kit.
Runs at the hub before 10:00 PM, and phones back before 7:00 AM, every night.
The Thursday count: every difference explained the same day.
Phones that moved without your approval: zero. Days the spare pool was under ten percent.
handbook.call: Moharam, for the schedule, a late run, or anything you cannot settle. The IT Manager for a phone that will not enroll, or lost mode on a missing phone. Ahmed Alaa for money and the buying list. Youssef Medhat for a flag. Mano for papers. An injury or the police: Moharam, then Adham.
